results.question: Can someone use an incoming viewing key to identify the shielded sender or spend my ZEC?
results.answer:
No. An **incoming viewing key (IVK)** cannot spend your ZEC. Spending needs a spending key (or recovery phrase). Viewing keys only let someone *read* some shielded data; they never grant spending authority ([ZIP 310](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0310), [ZIP 316](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0316)).

With an IVK, a scanner can see notes you received: amounts, which of your diversified addresses got them, memos, and that you can spend those notes. It does **not** by itself identify the shielded sender, and it does not tell whether those notes were later spent. A memo might *claim* a sender, but that claim is not automatically authenticated. A **full viewing key (FVK)** can additionally detect spends of known notes and recover some outgoing details when the sender used the expected outgoing viewing key—still without spending power.

Privacy also depends on wallets, pools, and network metadata; not every Zcash transfer is shielded ([how Zcash privacy works](https://z.cash/learn/how-to-use-zcash/)). Never paste viewing keys, spending keys, or seed phrases into chat.

results.question: Continue with an example.
results.answer:
Suppose Alice shares only her **incoming viewing key** (IVK) with an accountant. The accountant can scan the chain and see that Alice received, say, 2 ZEC to one of her shielded receivers, plus any memo the sender attached—without being able to spend those coins ([ZIP 310](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0310), [ZIP 316](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0316)).

results.question: Explain what an incoming viewing key can reveal in two sentences.
results.answer: An incoming viewing key reveals received note amounts, recipient addresses, and memos, but it does not grant spending authority and does not by itself identify the shielded sender or show whether those notes were spent. A full viewing key is different: it can also detect spending of known notes and recover outgoing payment details when the sender uses the expected outgoing viewing key ([ZIP 310](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0310), [ZIP 316](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0316)).

sources.title: ZIP 316: Unified Addresses and Unified Viewing Keys

results.question: Continue with an example.
results.answer:
Suppose Alice gives Bob only her incoming viewing key. When a shielded payment arrives, Bob can see the amount, which of Alice’s addresses received it, and the memo. He still cannot tell who sent it from the protocol alone, and he cannot later see whether Alice spent that note.

A memo might say “sent by Carol,” but that text is not proof. Detecting the spend would require a full viewing key, which can derive the note’s nullifier ([ZIP 310](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0310)).

sources.title: ZIP 310: Security Properties of Sapling Viewing Keys

results.question: yes
results.answer:
Suppose Alice shares a viewing key with auditor Ian, but not her spending key. With only her **incoming viewing key** (IVK), Ian can see notes she received: amounts, which of her addresses they went to, and memos. He cannot tell whether she later spent those notes, and a memo that names a sender is not proof of who sent them. [ZIP 310](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0310)

With her **full viewing key** (FVK), Ian can also detect when those known notes are spent, and recover outgoing payment details when Alice uses the expected outgoing viewing key. An FVK still cannot spend funds, and it does not reveal every counterparty or every transaction. [ZIP 310](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0310) Unified keys (UIVK and UFVK) bundle the same incoming-versus-full split across supported receivers. [ZIP 316](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0316)

sources.title: ZIP 310: Security Properties of Sapling Viewing Keys
ZIP 316: Unified Addresses and Unified Viewing Keys
